courses.name: General Physics II
weekTopics: Magnetic flux Φ_B = ∫B·dA = B*A*cos θ, measured in webers (Wb = T·m² = V·s), where θ is the angle between B and the OUTWARD NORMAL to the loop's plane — flux is maximum (BA) when the loop's plane is perpendicular to B and zero when the field lies in the plane of the loop.

Faraday's law of induction, ε = −N dΦ_B/dt in volts: the emf induced in a closed loop equals the negative of the time rate of change of the flux linking it, valid whether the change is caused by a changing B, by a changing enclosed area, by a changing orientation, or by any combination; the average emf over a stated interval is N|ΔΦ_B|/Δt, which is not the peak or instantaneous value.

Faraday's own conclusion that the mere existence of magnetic flux is not sufficient to induce an emf — the flux must be CHANGING — so a stationary magnet inside a loop, or a loop moving entirely within a uniform field, produces no current however large the flux.

Lenz's law as the physical content of the minus sign: the induced current flows in the sense whose magnetic field opposes the CHANGE in flux through the enclosed area, giving the deck's three rules (induced field opposite to B when the external flux is increasing, along B when it is decreasing, zero when the flux is constant), with the sense of the current then read off by the right-hand grip rule and only the field within the loop counted.

Motional emf |ε| = B*L*v for a rod of length L sliding at speed v on rails with B perpendicular to the circuit plane, giving I = BLv/R and a retarding force F = B*I*L = B²L²v/R that always opposes the motion, so that the mechanical power Fv = B²L²v²/R exactly equals the I²R dissipated — the energy-conservation argument behind Lenz's law.

The a.c. generator: an N-turn coil of area A rotating at angular speed ω = 2πf in a uniform field gives Φ_B = BA cos(ωt) and ε = N*B*A*ω*sin(ωt), with ε_peak = NBAω, ε_rms = ε_peak/√2 and a full-cycle average of exactly zero; the emf is zero when the flux is maximum and maximum when the flux is zero.

Charge circulated by a flux change, q = ∫I dt = N|ΔΦ_B|/R coulombs, which depends only on the total flux change and the circuit resistance and NOT on how quickly the change occurs — a faster change simply gives a larger current for a proportionately shorter time.

courses.name: Elementary Mathematics II (Calculus)
weekTopics: Applications of the definite integral to volumes: a region in the plane revolved about a fixed line (the axis of revolution) generates a solid of revolution whose volume is obtained by slicing it into thin pieces and integrating the cross-sectional area, V = ∫ₐᵇ A(s) ds.

The deck's four-step setup procedure: sketch the region and identify the axis of revolution (which fixes the variable of integration), sketch the cross-section as a disc, washer or shell and choose the matching formula, determine the boundaries of the solid, then set up and evaluate the definite integral.

The disc method, V = π∫ₐᵇ[f(x)]²dx about a horizontal axis (and π∫[g(y)]²dy about a vertical one), valid only when the region is flush against the axis so every cross-section is a full circle with no cavity.

The washer method, V = π∫ₐᵇ([R]² − [r]²)ds, with R the distance from the axis to the boundary farthest from it and r the distance to the nearest boundary, used whenever the region is offset from the axis; the standing trap of writing π∫(R − r)² instead of π∫(R² − r²) is treated explicitly.

The shell method, V = 2π∫ₐᵇ(radius)(height)ds, derived from unrolling a thin cylindrical shell into a rectangle of length 2π·radius, with the radius entering to the first power only; shells integrate in the variable opposite to the one used by discs and washers for the same axis.

Rotation about lines other than the coordinate axes — y = k and x = h — where every radius must be rewritten as a distance (f(x) − k, |x − h|) before squaring, and where the outer radius may belong to the lower curve when the axis lies above the region.

Practical setup skills: locating the limits by solving the bounding curves simultaneously, choosing between integrating in x and in y (including inverting y = f(x) to x = g(y)), splitting a region when the bounding curve changes partway, cross-checking a shell answer against a washer answer, and recognising a negative result as a swapped pair of radii.

courses.name: Introduction to Problem Solving
weekTopics: Modularisation is defined as the process of dividing a program's functionality into independent modules such that each independent module has everything it needs to implement only a part of the program's functionality, and decomposition is shown to be embedded in that definition, since separating an application's code into different modules and functions is itself the act of decomposing it.

The motivation is developed from the five-thousand-line function that cannot be changed safely because a change to one part affects other parts, and is set against the deck's five stated advantages of modularisation (parallel work by several people, easier management and extension, easier understanding of small units, reuse within the program or in another program, and faster design, development, testing and publishing) and its five stated disadvantages (longer execution time, increased storage size, longer compilation and loading time, increased inter-module communication problems, and more initial design time).

Module independence is presented through the single responsibility principle, which demands that a module have no more than one responsibility and not depend on other modules, and is measured by two quantities the students must be able to state exactly: cohesion, the extent to which the functions in a module work together to achieve the ultimate aim of the module, which should be high, and coupling, the extent to which modules depend on other modules before performing their function, which should be low; a car's steering wheel, radiator, battery and brake serve as the worked analogy.

Information hiding requires that the data structures and processing details of one module not be accessible to other modules and that modules pass only that much information as is required to accomplish the software functions, with three benefits: communication through controlled interfaces, a decreased probability of adverse effects, and restriction of the effects of a change in one component on other components.

Refactoring is defined as modifying a software system to improve the internal structure of the design without changing its external behaviour, checking the existing design for flaws such as redundancy and poorly constructed algorithms and data structures, and is illustrated by splitting a component that performs four weakly related functions into four components each exhibiting high cohesion, which yields easier integration, testing and maintenance.

Structural partitioning applies to hierarchical architectural styles and comes in two forms: horizontal, in which control modules communicate between functions and execute them at the cost of passing more data across module interfaces and a more complex control flow, and vertical, in which top-level control modules perform decision-making and little processing while low-level worker modules perform all input, computation and output; its benefits are easier testing and maintenance, slowly spreading negative impacts, and easy extension.

The second deck defines software architecture as the structure of the system containing the components of a program or system, the attributes or properties of those components and the relationships between them, explains why architecture matters for stakeholder communication, early design decisions and intellectual models of the system, and then distinguishes the three levels of software pattern (high-level architectural patterns often considered equivalent to software architecture, medium-level design patterns often considered equivalent to software components, and low-level language-specific idioms termed coding patterns) before contrasting the two generic design approaches, top-down for systems designed from scratch with unknown details and bottom-up for systems built from an existing system's primitives with abstraction increasing at each higher level, neither of which is individually practicable.

courses.name: General Physics Practical II
weekTopics: Determination of the magnetic permeability of free space μ₀ from the axial magnetic field of a single-turn circular loop, using the working formula B(z) = μ₀ I R² / [2 (R² + z²)^(3/2)], where B(z) is the flux density in tesla at axial distance z (m) from the centre, I is the loop current in amperes, R is the loop radius in metres, and μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A ≡ 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m; at z = 0 this reduces to the maximum value B(0) = μ₀I/2R.

Apparatus: a circular loop of radius R, a DC power supply, an ammeter, a movable magnetic (Hall) probe and a tesla meter; the virtual rig defaults to Coil 1 with R = 0.10 m and a current set to I = 1 A.

Procedure: place the probe at the centre of the coil (z = 0) and record B on the tesla meter, then increase z in steps of 2 cm (2, 4, 6 … up to 38 cm) recording B each time for 20 readings in all, and repeat the whole set for Coil 2, Coil 3 etc. of different radius — the 20 readings supply the spread of points needed for a straight-line fit and average out reading scatter, while the different coils test that μ₀ is independent of R and I.

Data analysis: for every reading compute the factor x = I R² / [2 (R² + z²)^(3/2)] in A/m, plot B (y-axis, in tesla) against that factor (x-axis, in A/m) to obtain the straight line B = μ₀x through the origin in the form y = mx, and take the gradient m = ΔB/Δx, which equals μ₀ directly in T·m/A = H/m; if the factor is computed without I the gradient equals μ₀I instead and μ₀ = gradient / I.

Unit handling and errors: the downloaded Excel sheet lists z in cm and B in nT while R is in metres, so z must be divided by 100 and B multiplied by 10⁻⁹ before plotting or the gradient is out by about 10⁹; systematic errors come from probe misalignment off the axis, a mislocated z = 0 origin, tesla-meter zero error, stray fields (Earth's field, nearby magnets or steel) and ammeter calibration, while random reading scatter is reduced by using the line of best fit over all 20 points.

Deck faults to flag: the B(z) equation and the analysis 'factor' appear only as dropped images, the slide heading is truncated at 'Magnetic-Permeability-of-', the sample data table skips from z = 10 cm to z = 26 cm, μ₀ is quoted as T·m/A in the theory slide but H/m in the summary (equivalent units, not a contradiction), and the summary sheet misprints 'REPUTATION between like poles' for REPULSION.

courses.name: Nigerian Peoples and Culture
weekTopics: The "Makers of Nigeria" deck profiles nine Nigerians from politics, activism, literature, music, law and sport, opening with Herbert Macaulay (1864-1946), tagged the father of Nigerian nationalism, who protested colonial water rates, land issues and railway finance management in the 1920s and founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party in 1923 as Nigeria's first political party, whose members were the first to sit in the legislative council and which merged with the Nigerian Youth Movement in the late 1930s to form the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons.

Obafemi Awolowo (1909-1987) is presented as first premier of the western region from 1954 to 1960, Nigeria's foremost federalist and leader of the Action Group whose campaign for a federal constitution was realised in the 1954 Lyleton Constitution, and as leader of the opposition against the Balewa-led government under the Northern People's Party, while Nnamdi Azikiwe (1904-1996) is given as the last governor-general from 1960 to 1963, the first elected president from 1963 to 1966 in the first republic, a co-founder of the NCNC who joined politics in 1944 and the inspiration for the radical multi-ethnic Zikist movement.

Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti (1900-1978), the "Lioness of Lisabi", mobilised market women and organised the 1953 Abeokuta conference that produced the Federation of Nigerian Women's Societies, and died on 13 April 1978 from injuries sustained when, aged 76, she was thrown from a second-story window during the 18 February 1977 military raid on the Lagos residence of her son Fela Anikulapo-Kuti (1938-1997), credited as the creator of Afrobeat in the early 1970s.

Chinua Achebe (1930-2013) is covered for Things Fall Apart (1958), the most widely read book in modern African literature, for heading the Biafra Broadcasting Service, and for becoming deputy national vice president of the People's Redemption Party in 1983 and writing The Trouble with Nigeria; Wole Soyinka (1934-Present) for his 22-month imprisonment in 1967 as a 33-year-old graduate, his flight from treason charges in 1994, and the 1986 Nobel Prize for Literature as the first African, dedicated to the imprisoned Nelson Mandela.

The deck closes with Gani (Ganiyu Oyesola) Fawehinmi (1938-2009), who began practising in Lagos in 1965, became known as "the people's lawyer" through pro bono work, campaigned on human rights for 40 years and pressed to re-open the case of Dele Giwa, killed by a parcel bomb in 1986, before dying of cancer in 2009; and Nwankwo Kanu (1976-Present), whose contribution won Nigeria the 1996 Olympic Gold medal past Brazil and Argentina, who won the African Footballer award, the Premier League, the UEFA Champions League and the UEFA Cup, and who serves as a UNICEF ambassador.

The Week 11 Summary PDF pairs the Makers of Nigeria with a Nigerian diaspora strand covering remittances as a key source of foreign exchange and major contributor to GDP, the diaspora's roots in pre-modern migrations, the slave trade and contemporary economic migration, the educational and professional achievements of Nigerians in the United States, the concept of "Japa", and the need for strategies to harness diaspora potential while addressing criminal activity by a minority; the closing slide also names Burna Boy, Wizkid, Davido and Rema.

The three learning objectives (practising paraphrasing, summarising and asking clarifying questions; applying listening skills in professional environments; critically analysing the impact of effective and ineffective listening on interpersonal and group interactions) and the six skills claimed as acquired: Active Engagement, Critical Listening, Cultural Competence, Note-Taking Mastery, Empathetic Communication, Continuous Improvement.

courses.name: Introduction to Web Technologies
weekTopics: Web application security terminology separating a vulnerability (a weakness in design, implementation or configuration) from a threat (potential harm), with security defined as protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data.

The five named vulnerabilities — SQL Injection (malicious SQL in user input manipulating the database, e.g. 'OR 1=1--'), Cross-Site Scripting (scripts injected into pages other users view, causing data theft or session hijacking), Cross-Site Request Forgery (tricking an already-authenticated user into an unwanted action), other Injection Attacks (Command Injection, XML Injection), and Security Misconfiguration (e.g. plaintext database credentials in config files).

Seven best practices matched to the vulnerabilities they answer: Input Validation with parameterised queries against SQLi, Output Encoding with Content Security Policy against XSS, Authentication and Authorization with 2FA and role/permission-based privileges, Session Management with unique tokens and expiry against CSRF, Security Headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options), Regular Updates and Security Testing (vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, code reviews); plus the Web Application Firewall as an additional layer filtering and monitoring HTTP/HTTPS requests, and secure development via Secure Coding, Code Review and DevSecOps.

Server deployment and hosting: server, deployment and hosting defined separately; physical versus virtual servers; server operating systems (Ubuntu, CentOS, Windows Server) and server roles (Apache/Nginx, MySQL/PostgreSQL, Microsoft Exchange); and the four hosting options — on-premises (complete control, heavy maintenance), cloud on AWS/Azure/GCP (scalability, flexibility, cost-efficiency, e.g. AWS Elastic Beanstalk), VPS (a partitioned physical server balancing control and cost, e.g. DigitalOcean) and shared hosting (cheapest, limited performance, e.g. Bluehost).

Scalability and performance optimisation: horizontal scaling (adding machines/instances, achieved by load balancing) versus vertical scaling (upgrading CPU, memory or storage on the existing server), load balancing with NGINX or AWS Elastic Load Balancing to remove bottlenecks and add fault tolerance, caching in a temporary layer, CDNs such as Cloudflare delivering content from servers closer to users, database optimisation through indexing, and front-end optimisation through minification, responsive images and lazy loading.

Monitoring, debugging, testing and continuous integration: monitoring through metrics, alerts and logging (New Relic, Datadog), debugging through error handling, debugging tools such as Chrome DevTools and version control with Git, load testing with Apache JMeter and Gatling, unit/integration/end-to-end testing, and CI pipelines with Jenkins or Travis CI that build, test and deploy on each commit; plus server security and maintenance measures — firewalls, patching, intrusion detection systems, strong authentication, backups and a disaster recovery plan.
